## Split cs tag generation into a single rule with cs-tagger; harden cs-tagger strictness

```
level: high
date: 2026-10-12
cross-repo: de_novo_assembly_0921, cs-tagger
```

### description

Cross-repo mirror: the requirement was made in de_novo_assembly_0921; the primary entry (full description, result, change) lives in that repo's docs/misc/requirements_audit.qmd. This repo's part: adopt the strict cs definition in the failure paths — error instead of silently truncating or dropping tokens.

### result

1. Refactored generate_cs_tag: bounds overruns (M/=/X, X, Ins, Del) now error naming the record and op; the previous `break`-truncation emitted a cs that silently disagreed with the CIGAR.
2. Refactored RefSkip: N ops shorter than 4 (or overrunning the reference) now error; the previous guard dropped the ~ intron token silently.
3. Added 5 unit tests; 24/24 pass. The strict build reproduces the de_novo normalizer's cs tags byte-identically (56/56 mapped records — in-bounds input is unaffected).

### change

Files updated: src/main.rs (strictness + tests).
Git: fix commit on `main`; no push. Packages: none. Environments: none.

## Diagnose bioconda PR 70178 CI failure (cs-tagger 0.3.1 bump)

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-15
```

### description

Debug why the BiocondaBot autobump PR updating the cs-tagger conda recipe from 0.3.0 to 0.3.1 fails CI, and state what the fix is.

### result

1. Answered - the Linux Tests build fails at build.sh line 14 (`cd cs-tagger`): the flatten-to-root restructure landed between tags v0.3.0 and v0.3.1, so the v0.3.1 source tarball no longer contains a nested `cs-tagger/` directory; conda_build.sh exits 1 under errexit.
2. Answered - two more old-layout paths must be fixed in the same pass: build.sh writes THIRDPARTY.yml to `${SRC_DIR}/cs-tagger/THIRDPARTY.yml` and meta.yaml license_file lists `cs-tagger/THIRDPARTY.yml`.
3. Answered - the vendoring workaround still applies: rust-htslib 1.0.1's Cargo.toml still carries the exact `features = ["bindgen"]` string the sed rewrites (verified from the 1.0.1 crate), and hts-sys stays 2.2.0.

### change

None (read-only diagnosis; evidence: PR 70178 job logs, tag trees, recipe files).

## Explain PR 70316 CI failure and Mergify comment; recover the fix path

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-15
```

### description

Explain why PR 70316's CI failed and what the Mergify checkbox comment means, then get the recipe-fix PR onto a path that can actually go green.

### result

1. Answered - the Lint job on PR 70316 crashed before linting any recipe: bioconda-utils runs `git merge-base origin/bump/cs_tagger HEAD` and the runner clone lacks that ref, so git exits 128. Deterministic for PRs whose base is not master; Linux/OSX tests were skipped for the same reason.
2. Answered - the comment is Mergify's generic queue control: ticking the box (or `@mergifyio queue`) asks Mergify to merge the PR automatically once required checks pass; it is not an error and did nothing while Lint was red.
3. Refactored - found in .mergify.yml that autobump auto-merge requires all commits authored by BiocondaBot and a PR younger than 3 days; #70178 has aged out either way, so the sub-PR route was a dead end. Retargeted PR 70316 to master (title/body rewritten as a standalone 0.3.1 update), pushed empty commit c64b962 to retrigger CI (re-run was denied: needs admin), and verified fresh Lint/ARM runs started. Background watch armed for the verdict.

### change

Files: none local beyond docs. External: PR 70316 retargeted to master + retitled; fork branch bumped to c64b962.
Git: none in this repo beyond docs. Packages: none. Environments: none.
